scenes.heading: Writing a contract that protects your writing business

sents.d: Writing a contract that protects your writing business
A short written agreement prevents most common client disputes.
A basic writing contract should define the deliverable (word count or scope), number of revision rounds included, payment terms and schedule, and deadline expectations on both sides.

Clarifying ownership and usage rights matters especially in writing — will the piece be published under your byline, anonymously, or under the client's name (ghostwritten) — since this affects both pricing and what you can later include in your own portfolio.
Requiring a deposit before starting, with the balance due on delivery or shortly after, is standard practice and protects against being left unpaid after completing the work.

take: Define scope, rights and payment, and take a deposit.
